title: Regional surge mitigation kickoff - notes and runbook draft
content:
Weekly kickoff notes: regional surge mitigation (10/07/2027)

Attendees: Priya (chair), Ethan, María, Samir, Louise, Alex, SRE oncall (Jonas)

Purpose: rapid alignment on a proactive playbook to handle expected customer-driven surge in SouthEast-Asia and EU-West triggered by partner product launches. Goal is to keep 99th percentile tail latency < 320ms for hosted-api critical routes while minimizing expensive burst capacity usage.

TL;DR summary:
- Observed signal: partner Beta customer will flip a feature flag on Oct 12 causing ~3x request volume for short bursts (6-18 hour windows) in APAC and a smaller mirrored burst in EU-West. Partner estimate: 120k tokens/min peak per region (internal estimate).
- Risk vector: sustained priming of KV caches + long context prompts will create burst cost and throttling for best-effort tenants unless hedged.
- Decision: implement a 3-layer mitigation strategy: (1) regional warm pools + pre-warming schedule, (2) smart fallback routing to cheaper quantized model variant under high spool, (3) soft-SLA throttles and circuit-breaker alerting.

Observed signals / data points:
- Baseline regional capacity (APAC-east): 320 vGPU-equivalent slots, average utilization 58% last 7d, spikes up to 85% during local business hours.
- Existing warm-pool coverage: ~40% of critical routes have cached prefixes; priming latency median 90ms, p95 420ms under warm-pool miss.
- Recent prewarm experiment (Sept): prewarmed + small-KV retention reduced p95 by ~120ms and decreased token-cost by ~6% for that route.

Playbook (draft):
1) Pre-warm schedule and criteria:
   - Create a region-level cron job that pre-warms top-40 routes by historical daily-90th traffic at 00:00 and 08:00 local time for 48 hours around expected surge window (Oct 12-14).
   - Prewarm VMs should be pinned to the customer's affinity pool where possible (dedicated reserved lanes).
   - Metric to watch: prewarm-hit-rate target > 70% on warmed routes. If < 50% at T+2h, escalate to infra lead.

2) Autoscaling / hedging rules:
   - Temporarily lower autoscaler cooldown to 30s for APAC-east and EU-west during surge windows to allow faster ramp-up of worker pools.
   - Reserve a 15% hedging buffer (non-burst capacity) by reducing vendor autoscale max-to-commit ratio for unrelated best-effort workloads during surge window.
   - If queue length > 400 or avg CPU-GPU saturation > 90% for 5m, enable fast-fallback routing (see #3).

3) Fast-fallback routing and model variants:
   - Route non-sensitive requests to quantized-2x variants (q8fn) with validated quality guardrails.
   - Routing policy: check tenant tier & route tag. Premium customers remain on standard model; all others eligible for fallback.
   - Implement gradual ramp: start with 10% fallback traffic, escalate to 50% if latency alarms persist.

4) Soft-SLA throttle & customer communications:
   - Threshold: p95 latency > 500ms or error rate > 1% sustained for 3min triggers throttle policy.
   - Throttle approach: return explanatory 429 with retry-after and degrade to cheaper variant when possible.
   - Draft customer-facing note (for CS): short blurb prepared for partner and affected customers describing planned mitigation and expected impact. CS to send 24h pre-surge.

5) Observability and alerting:
   - Dashboards: create surge-specific dashboard (APAC-east / EU-west) showing warm-pool-hit, queued-requests, p50/p95/p99 latency, token-rate, active-vGPUs.
   - New alerts: (a) warm-pool-hit < 50% for top-10 routes (b) queue length > 400 (c) GPU-utilization > 92% for 5m (d) fallback rollout > 25%

6) Oncall & escalation flow:
   - Primary: APAC infra oncall (Ethan) for first 30 mins. If unresolved, escalate to infra lead (Priya) and SRE manager (Louise).
   - War-room channel: #infra-regional-surge (create ephemeral) and link to runbook.

Experiment plan & tests (pre-surge, must finish by Oct 10):
- Synthetic traffic replay against mirror pool: run 2x expected peak for 1 hour and capture latency and eviction rates. Owner: Samir. Ticket: INF-2319.
- Warm-pool scaling smoke test: spin up pre-warm cron for 24h and validate hit-rate. Owner: María.
- Fallback routing dry run: route 5% of production-like traffic to q8fn variant in EU-west, compare quality delta and customer impact. Owner: Alex.

Action items (owner — due):
- Samir — run synthetic replay & attach results to INF-2319 (due 2027-10-09).
- María — enable temporary prewarm cron and validate metrics; update dashboard (due 2027-10-09).
- Alex — merge routing config change (PR #412) and coordinate canary (due 2027-10-10).
- Ethan — confirm autoscaler cooldown change & runbook steps with platform-engineering (due 2027-10-08).
- Louise — prepare CS blurb and post to #cs-notify (due 2027-10-11).
- Priya — finalize quick runbook and escalation matrix (due 2027-10-09).

Open questions & risks:
- Quality regression risk for fallback model (q8fn) on long-context prompts — need additional evals for customer-critical prompt sets. (Action: Alex add eval set by 10/08)
- Cost vs latency trade: hedging buffer reduces available capacity for other customers — need signoff from product on acceptable degradation. (Action: Priya schedule 30m with product-hosted-api)
- Inter-region capacity transfers may hit legal constraints for data residency on some tenants; ensure routing doesn't violate pinned regions. (Action: Ethan verify routing rules respect region pins)

Notes from discussion (free-form):
- Samir suggested building a lightweight heatmap of per-tenant priming cost to identify top offenders for directed throttles. Good short-term signal.
- María flagged a potential imbalance: EU-west has more prewarmed capacity per rack but less KV retention; suggested increasing retention TTL for warmed prefixes during surge windows.
- Louise reminded to have billing tags applied to all hedging resources for post-mortem cost allocation.

Appendix: quick checklist for surge window (to be attached to incident playbook)
- [ ] Enable prewarm cron in APAC-east & EU-west (scripts live in fleet-config repo: scripts/prewarm)
- [ ] Update autoscaler cooldown and commit hedging buffer
- [ ] Deploy routing PR #412 as canary (5% -> 25% -> 50%)
- [ ] Publish CS notice 24h before start
- [ ] Stand up war-room 30m prior to expected surge

Next sync: daily standup at 09:00 PT starting 2027-10-10 through 2027-10-14. Standup cadence: 15min, quick updates on metrics, blockers, and whether to escalate.

End of notes.

Document history: initial draft 2027-10-07 by Priya; edits 2027-10-08 (Samir added replay plan).
